claims.text: The ball-milled Mg-Al-Ti-V-Fe-Co powder is a nanocrystalline BCC solid solution.
The ball-milled powder may contain surface oxides acquired during milling.
SPS at 950 °C, within a 900-1000 °C range, for 10 minutes under 50 MPa with a 50-100 °C/min heating rate and vacuum or argon is an appropriate processing condition.
Increasing sintering temperature toward 1000 °C exponentially increases Al and Ti diffusion and promotes Al, Ti, and V redistribution.
Thermally activated diffusion produces Mg-Al-Ti intermetallic precipitates in the Mg-Al-Ti-V-Fe-Co alloy.
The precipitates are fine, coherent, likely Laves-type or complex cubic, and form a continuous network at grain boundaries and within the BCC matrix.
Phase separation is driven by the Mg-Al-Ti mixing enthalpy together with the high defect density introduced by ball milling.
The intermetallic precipitates impede dislocation motion and thereby increase hardness.
The secondary-phase network blocks oxygen and corrosion-ion transport and improves oxidation and corrosion resistance.
The precipitate network inhibits grain growth and produces Hall-Petch strengthening.
A sintering temperature near 950-1000 °C optimizes precipitation and densification without unacceptable magnesium loss.
Below 800 °C, diffusion and densification driving force are insufficient to form a continuous barrier network, resulting in lower density and hardness.
Above 1000 °C, magnesium sublimation causes composition deviation and porosity.
The proposed processing will produce a bulk alloy with relative density greater than 98%.
The proposed processing will produce Vickers hardness greater than 600 HV.
The corrosion current density in 3.5 wt% NaCl will be at least 50% lower than for a sample sintered at 800 °C.
The sintered alloy will retain a BCC matrix containing dispersed intermetallic precipitates and will develop a continuous passive oxide film.
An 800 °C baseline sample will have lower density, lower hardness, and higher corrosion rates than the 950 °C sample.
Magnesium loss above 1000 °C prevents formation of the proposed Mg-Al-Ti barrier phases and produces a porous, brittle material with degraded mechanical and corrosion performance.
Parabolic oxidation kinetics at 950 °C would indicate diffusion control, whereas linear kinetics after 1050 °C sintering would indicate loss of the protective diffusion barrier.

contradictions.description: The specified alloy contains Mg, Al, Ti, V, Fe, and Co but no Cr, while the structural mediator asserts formation of a Cr/Ti/Mg-rich passive film without identifying any chromium source or contamination route.
